lessons.title: He shall lift you up — completing Step 7 and receiving what was asked for
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When God lifted Joseph — from the pit, from Potiphar's house, from the prison — it was not because Joseph had managed his circumstances skillfully. It was because Joseph had remained in genuine submission through each descent. The pattern of Joseph's life is the covenant pattern of Step 7: the humbling precedes the lifting, and the lifting is God's action, not the result of the person's recovery of position. Step 7 completion is not a moment of arrival. It is the confirmation of a posture that the life will maintain — and the first experience of what God does when the posture is genuinely held.

Step 6 established something important: there are things in the character that human effort named but could not remove. That is not failure — it is the honest prerequisite for what this step asks.

When Peter stood on the day of Pentecost and told the crowd what to do, the first word he spoke was repent. Not believe harder. Not try again. Repent — and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins. The remission — the sending away — of sin is not accomplished by the decision of Step 3 alone. It is accomplished by the full covenant response: repentance, the name, and the Spirit. This is what the steps have been preparing the road toward.

HE SHALL LIFT YOU UP

"Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up." — James 4:10 KJV The lifting is not always immediately visible. It is not always dramatic. Often the first evidence of the lifting is internal — the release of what had been occupying the person that was not from God, and the quiet arrival of what is. The defect does not always disappear in a single transaction. What changes in Step 7 is the person's relationship to the defect — from owner to surrendered petitioner, from a thing being protected to a thing being released into God's hands for removal in His timing and by His method.

The tax collector in the temple did not lift his eyes toward heaven. He beat his breast and said: God be merciful to me a sinner. Jesus said he went home justified. Humility is not a performance. It is the honest posture of the person who knows what they are.

WHAT TO DO WITH WHAT REMAINS

Some defects will diminish quickly. Others will require ongoing surrender — the daily renewal of the Step 7 petition, the returning of what has returned, the repeated presentation of the thing to God because the self has taken it back. "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint." — Isaiah 40:31 KJV The waiting is not passive. It is the active posture of the person who has placed what they cannot remove in the hands of the One who can — and remains there. The strength renews in the waiting, not after the waiting is over. The mounting up, the running, the walking without fainting — these happen to the person who has learned to wait in the posture of humility rather than returning to self-management when the removal does not come on the self's schedule.

THE DAILY PETITION

Step 7 is not complete when the prayer is prayed once. It is the beginning of a daily petition — the ongoing presentation of the defects to God, the daily renewal of the willingness expressed in Step 6, the repeated choice not to take back what has been surrendered. Each morning: name the primary defect. Confirm the willingness. Ask for the removal. Then walk through the day in the posture of a person who has placed what they cannot carry in the hands of the One who can.

THE ROAD FORWARD

The pattern is consistent across the whole of Scripture: God lifts those who humble themselves. Not those who perform humility — those who actually occupy the low place honestly. The lifting is always in response to the genuine posture, never to the performance of it.

Step 7 has established the posture. Steps 8 and 9 move the work outward — from the internal life to the relational field. The person who has genuinely humbled themselves before God in Step 7 is positioned for the reconciliation that Steps 8 and 9 require — because the pride that resists reconciliation has been addressed at its source.

The person who has genuinely asked God to remove what they could not remove has done something they could not undo. They have acknowledged in the most specific possible way what is true: they cannot complete themselves. And God, who is faithful to that kind of honesty, lifts what is brought to Him.

The prayer established in this step becomes the ongoing contact of Step 11. What begins here as a request becomes a relationship.

What has been asked for in this step is not merely the removal of defects. It is the entrance of the God who can sustain what the defects have been blocking. Acts records consistently what that entrance looks like and the evidence that it has occurred. The person who completes Step 7 honestly is not far from the threshold that the remainder of the curriculum is building toward.

TEACHER NOTES

The goal is honest assessment of what the Step 7 petition produced — not performance of transformation, but honest naming of what changed and what remains. lessons.title: If thou bring thy gift to the altar — the list of all persons harmed and the willing heart
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Zacchaeus came down from the sycamore tree and received Jesus into his house, he did not wait to be prompted about restitution. The encounter with genuine grace produced an immediate outward movement: "Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold." The internal work had reached the relational field. That is Step 8. Step 8 is not the amends. Step 8 is the list and the willing heart. Both must be present before Step 9 can begin.

In Step 7 we arrived at the honest admission that some things require more than human effort — they require what only God can provide. Step 8 is where the changed person begins to address what the old life left behind.

The God who governs the life now is one Spirit, one LORD — and the same God who empowers the amends is the same God who produced the change that makes the amends honest.

The person who bears God's name — who has been surnamed by God — carries that identity into every relationship they address. The amends of Step 8 is not merely making things right. It is the action of a person who is now living under a different name and therefore acting differently than the person who made the original harm.

The amends list is the ledger of genuine repentance made concrete in relationship. Repentance that does not move toward those who were harmed has stopped short of what repentance actually is. Step 8 is where the turn of the heart produces the list that Step 9 will walk.

THE LIST

"Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift." — Matthew 5:23-24 KJV The list already exists. It was written in Step 4 — the harms column, the names, the specific things that happened. Step 8 takes that list and reviews it through a single lens: who has something against me, and am I willing to go? Review every name. Add any that the writing of Step 4 did not surface but that the journey through Steps 5, 6, and 7 has revealed. The list is not an indictment — it is the preparation for reconciliation. The goal of every name on the list is not punishment of the self but the restoration of what was damaged.

Zacchaeus was small of stature and up a tree — literally elevated above the crowd, disconnected from the level ground of honest encounter. Jesus stopped beneath that tree and called him down by name.

THE WILLING HEART — WHERE MOST PEOPLE STALL

The list is the easier part. The willing heart is where Step 8 actually does its work. For most people there will be names on the list toward which the willingness does not come naturally. The harm was mutual. The resentment is still present. The person is unreachable, deceased, or in a situation where contact would cause further harm. "And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you." — Ephesians 4:32 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Ephesus — describing the character of the person walking in the Spirit. The willingness for reconciliation is not generated by the self. It is the fruit of what the Spirit produces in the person who has genuinely received the forgiveness that Ephesians 4:32 describes. The person who has been forgiven much is capable of forgiving much. The inventory of what has been forgiven in Steps 4 and 5 is the ground from which the willingness for Step 8 grows.

For every name toward which willingness does not come: bring it to the Step 7 petition. Ask God for the willingness. The willingness is the fruit of the Spirit — it can be asked for and received before the amends is made.

LEVITICUS 6 — THE RESTITUTION PRINCIPLE

"Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found, Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto." — Leviticus 6:4-5 KJV The principle of restitution runs from the Law through the Gospels — Zacchaeus restoring fourfold, Jesus requiring reconciliation before the gift at the altar. Where restitution is possible it is part of the willing heart. What was taken should be returned if possible. What was damaged should be repaired if possible. The willing heart includes the willingness to restore, not only to apologize.

THE ROAD FORWARD

Scripture shows that the changed life produces changed action. This is not the root — it is the fruit. The amends list is not the source of the transformation. It is the evidence of it. What God has genuinely changed will move toward what it previously damaged.

The list is complete. The heart is willing — or willing to become willing through the Step 7 petition. Step 9 is the going. THE NAME UNDER WHICH THE AMENDS IS MADE "And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him." — Colossians 3:17 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Colosse — giving the governing principle for all action: whatsoever you do, in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus. The name governs the action. Not only the formal religious action — every word, every deed. The amends conversation is a word and a deed. It is done in a name. The name under which the amends is made determines its quality and its source. The amends made from guilt is made in a different name than the amends made from genuine love of God and neighbor. The amends made to repair the self's reputation is made in a different name than the amends made in obedience to the God who requires reconciliation before the gift at the altar. Do the amends in His name. Not yours.

CALLED BY HIS NAME — THE COVENANT MARK

"If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land." — 2 Chronicles 7:14 KJV My people — called by my name. The covenant mark in the old covenant was the name of God placed on a people. To be called by His name was to carry His identity, to be distinguished from the surrounding world, to bear the mark of belonging to Him rather than to the world. The amends of Steps 8 and 9 is the practical expression of what it means to live as a person called by His name. The name is not only an identity marker — it is a covenant obligation. To bear the name of God is to live in a way that honors what the name means. The reconciliation that Steps 8 and 9 require is the outworking of the covenant obligation that comes with bearing His name.

The curriculum will continue to trace where the name of God in the new covenant is placed — and what it means for the person on whom it rests. For now: what does it mean that you are called by His name — and what does that name require of you in the amends you are about to make?

The list is not a punishment. It is the record of a person who has been genuinely changed and is now taking inventory of what the old life owed. The identity that produces the list is already different from the identity that created the debts.

The list matters. The willingness matters more. Step 9 is where the willingness becomes action — and where the relational ground of the old life begins to be cleared.

The pattern Acts records — of people who have been genuinely changed producing genuine action toward those they have harmed — is not incidental. Zacchaeus did not offer restitution because he was told to. He offered it because the change produced the action. That is the testimony of every person in this step.

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ Matthew 5:23-24 KJV — "Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift."

ASSIGNMENT

The Step 8 list 1. Pull out the harms column from Step 4. Review every name. 2. Mark each name: willing / conditionally willing / not yet willing. 3. For every conditional or not yet entry — write what the resistance is protecting. 4. Begin the Step 7 petition for the names toward which willingness has not yet come: ask God for the willingness. Due: Before Lesson 2

lessons.title: And rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee — becoming willing for every name
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Jesus told the story of the servant who owed ten thousand talents and was forgiven — and then went and seized his fellow servant who owed a hundred pence — the master's response was not indifference. He delivered the unforgiving servant to the tormentors until the debt was paid. The parable is not about the debt. It is about the capacity for forgiveness in a person who has received it. The person who has genuinely received forgiveness is capable of extending it. The person who cannot extend it has not fully received it. Step 8 Lesson 2 addresses the names on the list toward which the willing heart has not yet arrived. This is where the real work of Step 8 happens.

In Step 7 we arrived at the honest admission that some things require more than human effort — they require what only God can provide. Step 8 is where the changed person begins to address what the old life left behind.

The amends list is the ledger of genuine repentance made concrete in relationship. Repentance that does not move toward those who were harmed has stopped short of what repentance actually is. Step 8 is where the turn of the heart produces the list that Step 9 will walk.

BECOMING WILLING

The willingness for the difficult name on the list is not manufactured by effort. It is the fruit of having received forgiveness — and the honest examination of whether what was received in Steps 4 and 5 has been fully accepted or only intellectually acknowledged. "And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses." — Mark 11:25 KJV Jesus said this to His disciples — people who were already following Him — showing them the connection between the forgiveness received and the forgiveness extended. connected to the forgiveness extended. Not because God is withholding — but because the person who cannot forgive has placed an obstacle between themselves and the capacity to receive what is freely offered.

WHAT BLOCKS THE HEART

The most common blocks to the willing heart in Step 8: The mutual harm. The person on the list also harmed me. This is true in many cases. The resentment column has their name in it for that reason. And their name is also in the harms column. Both are true. Step 8 concerns what I owe — not what they owe. Their accounting is their business. Mine is mine. The severity. What I did was too significant to address with an amends. The reverse is true: the more significant the harm the more urgently the amends is required. The weight of the unaddressed harm is being carried by the person who caused it. The amends is not primarily for the other person — it is the laying down of what the person carrying it can no longer afford to carry. The fear. They will reject the amends. They will use it against me. They will not receive it well. Step 9 will address the method — how to make the amends in a way that does not cause further harm. Step 8 is the willingness. The method is a Step 9 question. "And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you." — Ephesians 4:32 KJV The tenderhearted person — the person whose heart has been softened by the experience of genuine forgiveness — does not need to manufacture the willingness. It arises from having received what Ephesians 4:32 describes. If the willingness does not arise naturally it is the signal that the forgiveness received in Steps 4 and 5 has not been fully accepted. Return there. Receive more fully. The willingness follows.

THE ROAD FORWARD

Scripture shows that the changed life produces changed action. This is not the root — it is the fruit. The amends list is not the source of the transformation. It is the evidence of it. What God has genuinely changed will move toward what it previously damaged.

Every name on the list should now have a willing heart beside it — or the willingness is being actively asked for through the Step 7 petition. Lesson 3 prepares the conversation of Step 9. Do not begin the amends conversations without the preparation Lesson 3 provides.

RAHAB — THE PAST DOES NOT DISQUALIFY THE WILLING

Rahab was a harlot in Jericho. When the spies came she hid them and made a covenant with them — a scarlet cord hung from her window, a promise of protection. And when Jericho fell, her house stood. "By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace." — Hebrews 11:31 KJV The writer of Hebrews does not sanitize the description. She is identified precisely by the thing her neighbors would have named her by. The faith is named alongside the history — not instead of it. And she is in Hebrews 11 alongside Abraham and Moses and Noah — identified by the faith, not disqualified by what preceded it. Matthew's Gospel traces the lineage of Jesus and includes Rahab — a woman who had lived in a way that disqualified her from every list she would have been placed on by her contemporaries. In the genealogy of Christ. Named. Included. The scarlet cord she hung from the window — the mark of her covenant with the people of God — is a thread that runs from Jericho to the redemption of all things.

The person who believes their history disqualifies them from the amends list — whose willingness stalls at the weight of what they were before this program — Rahab is the answer. She was identified by what she had been. She acted by faith. The house stood. And she is in the lineage of the One who is the author of eternal salvation.

lessons.title: First be reconciled — what the amends conversation requires and what it does not
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Zacchaeus made restitution, the announcement preceded the action — he declared what he intended before he had done it. The declaration itself was part of the reconciliation. The amends conversation in Step 9 is not only an action — it is a specific kind of conversation that requires preparation. Step 8 Lesson 3 is that preparation.

In Step 7 we arrived at the honest admission that some things require more than human effort — they require what only God can provide. Step 8 is where the changed person begins to address what the old life left behind.

The amends list is the ledger of genuine repentance made concrete in relationship. Repentance that does not move toward those who were harmed has stopped short of what repentance actually is. Step 8 is where the turn of the heart produces the list that Step 9 will walk.

WHAT THE AMENDS CONVERSATION IS

The amends is not an apology. An apology is a statement about what the person feels — I'm sorry, I feel bad about what I did. The amends is a statement about what happened and what the person intends to do about it — I harmed you in this way, I am willing to make it right, and here is how I am changing. The amends conversation has three parts: 1. Name what happened — specifically, without minimizing or qualifying 2. Take full responsibility for your part — without referencing what the other person did 3. Where possible, offer to make it right — restore what was taken, repair what was damaged, repay what was owed

Zacchaeus was small of stature and up a tree — literally elevated above the crowd, disconnected from the level ground of honest encounter. Jesus stopped beneath that tree and called him down by name.

WHAT THE AMENDS CONVERSATION IS NOT

The amends is not an invitation to relitigate. Do not reference what the other person did. Do not use the amends conversation as an opportunity to share what the Step 4 inventory contained about their behavior. The amends is a one-direction conversation — what I did, what I am taking responsibility for, what I am willing to do differently. The amends is not a request for the other person's forgiveness. Forgiveness is theirs to give or withhold in their own time. The amends does not require a particular reception to be complete. The amends is complete when it has been honestly offered — regardless of how it is received. The amends is not a performance of transformation. It is not the opportunity to show the person how much the recovery program has changed you. The fruit of the transformation will speak for itself over time. The amends conversation is about what happened — not about what has changed.

CATEGORIES OF AMENDS

Direct amends: in person, to the person, naming specifically what happened. Written amends: for persons who are geographically unreachable, with whom contact would cause further harm, or in situations where the mentor has counseled that direct contact is inappropriate. Living amends: for deceased persons, or persons where any contact would cause harm to another party — the amends is made by becoming a different person in the area where the harm occurred, living differently in the ongoing life. Financial amends: where money was stolen, borrowed and not returned, or where material damage was caused. The financial amends may require a payment plan. Arrange it and keep it.

WHEN TO WAIT

Some amends must wait. The amends that would cause harm to a third party — revealing information that would damage an innocent person — waits until a method can be found that does not cause further harm. The amends that would expose the person legally may require consultation with the mentor and possibly legal counsel before proceeding. Do not wait indefinitely. Wait for the right method, not for the exemption.

THE ROAD FORWARD

Scripture shows that the changed life produces changed action. This is not the root — it is the fruit. The amends list is not the source of the transformation. It is the evidence of it. What God has genuinely changed will move toward what it previously damaged.

The conversation is prepared. Lesson 4 completes the step — the list is full, the heart is willing, the conversation is prepared, and the step is ready to move into Step 9.

The list is not a punishment. It is the record of a person who has been genuinely changed and is now taking inventory of what the old life owed. The identity that produces the list is already different from the identity that created the debts.

The list matters. The willingness matters more. Step 9 is where the willingness becomes action — and where the relational ground of the old life begins to be cleared.

Teach this clearly and return to it if the student defaults to apology language. COVENANT CONTEXT FOR THE TEACHER Zacchaeus — Luke 19:8 — made the announcement before the action. The intention of the amends is part of the reconciliation. Help students understand that the preparation of Step 8 Lesson 3 is itself the beginning of the ...

ASSIGNMENT

Categorize each amends: direct, written, living, or financial. For financial amends write the plan. 3. Identify any amends that require waiting and name what needs to be resolved before they proceed. 4. Review the full list with your m...

lessons.title: Then come and offer thy gift — completing Step 8 with a full list and a willing heart
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
The altar is ready. The gift is in hand. The brother has been remembered. Now the step is complete — not because the amends have been made but because the list is full, the heart is willing, and the conversation has been prepared. Step 8 is the readiness. Step 9 is the going.

THE COMPLETION OF STEP 8

The amends list is the ledger of genuine repentance made concrete in relationship. Repentance that does not move toward those who were harmed has stopped short of what repentance actually is. Step 8 is where the turn of the heart produces the list that Step 9 will walk.

In Step 7 we arrived at the honest admission that some things require more than human effort — they require what only God can provide. Step 8 is where the changed person begins to address what the old life left behind.

Step 8 is complete when three things are true:

The list is full. Every person the Step 4 inventory identified, every person the journey through Steps 5-7 revealed, every name the honest review of this step surfaced — all are on the list. The list is not a final judgment. It can be added to in Step 10 as the daily inventory reveals what Step 4 did not surface. But today, as of this lesson, every name that is known is on it. The heart is willing. For every name on the list, the willing heart is present — either arising naturally from what was received in Steps 4 and 5, or arriving through the Step 7 petition. No name is being withheld from willingness. What could not be reached through effort was reached through asking. The conversation is prepared. For the direct amends, the three-part structure has been practiced. For the written amends, the letter has been drafted. For the living amends, the specific change has been named. For the financial amends, the plan exists.

WHAT STEP 8 PREPARED

"And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work." — 2 Corinthians 9:8 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers at Corinth — showing them that the grace available to them is sufficient for every good work. The amends of Step 9 are a good work. The grace that is available to the person who has worked Steps 1 through 8 honestly is sufficient for what Step 9 requires. The resistance felt toward the most difficult names does not indicate insufficient grace. It indicates the grace has not yet been drawn upon for that specific thing. Draw upon it. It is there.

THE ROAD FORWARD

Scripture shows that the changed life produces changed action. This is not the root — it is the fruit. The amends list is not the source of the transformation. It is the evidence of it. What God has genuinely changed will move toward what it previously damaged.

Step 8 is done. Step 9 begins immediately. Do not delay. The list prepared in Step 8 grows heavier with time, not lighter. The amends conversation that was prepared in Lesson 3 is ready. The first appointment is made. Begin.

Zacchaeus was small of stature and up a tree — literally elevated above the crowd, disconnected from the level ground of honest encounter. Jesus stopped beneath that tree and called him down by name.

THE GIFT AT THE ALTAR — NOW

"Then come and offer thy gift." — Matthew 5:24 KJV The second half of the instruction has a first half: first be reconciled, then come and offer. The student who is completing Step 8 is in the position of the first half — the list is prepared, the heart is willing, the conversation is ready. The coming and offering of Step 9 is immediately ahead. Do not linger in the position of Step 8 when Step 9 is the next instruction. The altar is where you are going — after the reconciliation that Step 9 will complete. Step 8 is the preparation of the going. Step 9 is the going. The gift waits at the altar — and the altar waits for the going to be done.

THE GRACE SUFFICIENT FOR THE FIRST NAME

"My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." — 2 Corinthians 12:9 KJV Paul wrote this in the context of his own repeated petition for relief from something he could not remove — and the answer he received. God's strength is made perfect in the weakness that has been genuinely surrendered. The amends list contains exactly that kind of weakness — the honest naming of harm caused, the vulnerability of the three-part conversation, the not knowing how it will be received. The grace is not distributed after the amends is made. It is present in the weakness of making it. The person who walks into the most difficult amends conversation on the list is the person in whom God's strength is being made

perfect. The weakness that makes the amends hard is the same weakness that makes the grace sufficient. Step 8 ends at the door of Step 9. Walk through it.

The list is not a punishment. It is the record of a person who has been genuinely changed and is now taking inventory of what the old life owed. The identity that produces the list is already different from the identity that created the debts.

The list matters. The willingness matters more. Step 9 is where the willingness becomes action — and where the relational ground of the old life begins to be cleared.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 8 Lesson 4 MEMBER LESSON. This is the completion lesson. Its function is accountability and launch. Confirm the three completions — full list, willing heart, prepared conversation — and send the student into Step 9 immediately. COVENANT CONTEXT FOR THE TEACHER Matthew 5:24 — go thy way, first be reconciled, then come and offer. Step 8 is the preparation of the going. Step 9 is the going. The altar is ready. The gift is in hand. The step is done. Move. 2 CORINTHIANS 9:8 — HOW TO TEACH Fram...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ 2 Corinthians 9:8 KJV — "And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work."

ASSIGNMENT

Launch Step 9 1. Confirm the three completions with your mentor: full list, willing heart, prepared conversation. 2. Make the first appointment for a direct amends before you leave this lesson. 3. Complete the first amends this week. Report back to your mentor what happened. Due: Step 9 begins now GO THY WAY — FIRST BE RECONCILED TO THY BROTHER

lessons.title: Go thy way and be reconciled — the direct amends and how to make them
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Jesus restored Peter after the resurrection — three questions matching the three denials, the specific and unhurried addressing of each one — He did not summarize or abbreviate the reconciliation. He went to each one. The restoration required the specificity. The going is the step. Step 9 is the doing of what Step 8 prepared. The list is in hand. The heart is willing. The conversation is ready. Now go.

Step 8 produced a list and a willingness. Step 9 is where willingness becomes action.

The God who walks with the person through the amends is one Spirit, one LORD — fully present in the most uncomfortable conversations this program requires.

Colossians 3:17 KJV: "And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus." The amends of Step 9 are among the most concrete things the student will do in this program. The person doing them does so in the name of the Lord Jesus — not as a formula, but as an identity. This is who I am now. This is whose name I carry. This is how that name acts in relationship.

The amend is the evidence of the turn. Every person on the list represents a place where the old life reached into another life and left damage. The repentant person who has been genuinely changed does not leave that damage unaddressed. This is not penance — it is the natural direction of a life that has genuinely turned.

THE DIRECT AMENDS

"Go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift." — Matthew 5:24 KJV The instruction is to go. Not to wait for conditions to improve. Not to wait until the other person is also ready for reconciliation. Not to wait until the outcome can be predicted. Go. The going is the step — not the reception of the amends, not the outcome of the conversation, not whether the person forgives. The direct amends conversation has three parts — prepared in Step 8 Lesson 3: 1. Name what happened — specifically, without minimizing 2. Take full responsibility for your part 3. Where possible, offer to make it right Deliver all three. Do not stop at the first one. Do not allow the other person's reaction — positive or negative — to interrupt the delivery of all three parts. The amends is complete when all three have been honestly offered.

The prodigal rehearsed his speech the whole way home. The father did not wait for the speech. He saw his son while he was yet a great way off and ran to meet him. The amends is not the performance — it is the arrival.

WHEN IT IS RECEIVED WELL

Some amends will be received with grace — the other person is glad you came, the conversation produces connection, the relief is immediate and mutual. Receive this with gratitude and without surprise. God goes before the amends that is genuinely offered. "When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him." — Proverbs 16:7 KJV The person who has worked the steps honestly — who brings genuine humility and genuine accountability to the amends conversation — often finds that the reception is better than the fear predicted. This is not because the other person was easier than expected. It is because the posture of genuine reconciliation produces what the posture of self-protection cannot.

WHEN IT IS RECEIVED POORLY

Some amends will not be received well. The other person may be angry. They may use it against you. They may reject it entirely.

The amends is complete when it is honestly offered — regardless of how it is received. The outcome belongs to the other person. The offering belongs to you. Do not repeat the amends in the same conversation in response to a poor reception. Say it once, honestly. The living amends — the change of life that follows — is the longer conversation. The words are the beginning.

ZACCHAEUS — THE TREE, THE GROUND, AND THE RESTITUTION THAT PRECEDED THE REQUEST

Zacchaeus — the name means pure or innocent. Which he was not.

He was a chief tax collector in Jericho — which means he had spent years using the authority of Rome to take more than was owed and keep the surplus for himself. He was wealthy. He was hated. And he was small of stature in a crowd that had gathered around Jesus, so he climbed a sycamore tree to see above the heads of people who would not have made room for him at ground level.

The sycamore tree is worth noting. It was low enough to climb and strong enough to hold him. But it was also a position of elevation — above the crowd, disconnected from the level ground where honest encounter happens. Zacchaeus was watching from a distance, from a height, unable to be seen, unable to be close.

Jesus stopped under the tree. And said: "Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house." — Luke 19:5 KJV

He called him by name. The man who was supposed to be hiding. The man who had climbed above the crowd. Jesus looked up and called him down by name — and Zacchaeus came down immediately and received Him joyfully.

What happened next is the part that matters for Step 9. Before Jesus said anything about his past, before any instruction was given, before any demand was made — Zacchaeus stood and said: "Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold." — Luke 19:8 KJV

The amends came out of him before they were asked for. The genuine encounter with Jesus produced the genuine reckoning with what had been done. The restitution was not a religious duty performed under pressure. It was the natural response of a man who had just been named by the God who knew everything about him and still called him down.

Your Step 9 is not a religious duty. It is what happens when the encounter has been real. The genuine encounter produces the genuine reckoning. Go make it.

THE ROAD FORWARD

The pattern across Scripture is that genuine encounter with God produces restitution — not because it is demanded, but because the person who has been genuinely changed cannot rest in the debt. Zacchaeus gave back fourfold before Jesus said a word about it.

Go to the next name on the list. Do not wait between amends for the results of the previous one to settle. The list was prepared for the going, not for intermission. Move through it with the same consistency that built the list.

WHAT TO DO WHEN YOU FINISH THE CONVERSATION

When the amends conversation is complete — all three parts delivered, honestly — leave. Do not prolong the conversation looking for a better reception. Do not return to the subject in the same visit to add what was forgotten. If something was forgotten, address it in a separate conversation. The amends is a specific, bounded conversation that has a beginning and an end. The receipt of the amends — gratitude, anger, silence, rejection — belongs entirely to the other person. Your part ended when the three parts were honestly delivered. Thank them for receiving you, regardless of how they received the content. Then go to the next name on the list.

The person who has made honest amends is not the person who made the original harm. That person was governed by the bondage. This person is governed by something else — and the amends is the clearest possible evidence of the difference.

The relational ground cleared here does not need to be recultivated. Step 10 is the daily discipline that keeps what has been cleared from filling back in.

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ Proverbs 16:7 KJV — "When a man's ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him."

ASSIGNMENT

Make the first amends 1. Make the first direct amends this week. All three parts. 2. Write in your journal immediately after: what happened, what you said, how it was received, what you felt. 3. Schedule the second amends before the week ends. 4. Report to your mentor on what the first amends produced. Due: Before Lesson 2

lessons.title: The freedom of amends — what happens when relational debts are cleared
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Zacchaeus announced his restitution, Jesus said: "This day is salvation come to this house." Not eventually. Not after the restitution was completed and verified. This day. The going — the willing presentation of the amends — was the evidence of salvation that had already come. The freedom described in Step 9 Lesson 2 is not the reward at the end of the list. It is what begins arriving with the first amends honestly made.

Step 8 produced a list and a willingness. Step 9 is where willingness becomes action.

The amend is the evidence of the turn. Every person on the list represents a place where the old life reached into another life and left damage. The repentant person who has been genuinely changed does not leave that damage unaddressed. This is not penance — it is the natural direction of a life that has genuinely turned.

WHAT THE AMENDS PRODUCES IN THE PERSON MAKING IT

The most common surprise in Step 9 is what happens to the person making the amends — not what happens to the person receiving it. The weight that has been carried since the harm was caused begins to lift with the first honest conversation. Not because the other person's reception was positive. Because the carrying is over. The healing James 5:16 described — confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed — is operating here James wrote this to born-again believers — showing them the connection between honest acknowledgment and healing. The healing that James describes is not the healing of the person who receives the confession. It is the healing of the person who makes it. The fault confessed — the harm named honestly, the responsibility taken fully — begins the healing of the person who named it.

The prodigal rehearsed his speech the whole way home. The father did not wait for the speech. He saw his son while he was yet a great way off and ran to meet him. The amends is not the performance — it is the arrival.

THE CLEARING OF THE RELATIONAL FIELD

Each amends made clears a portion of the relational field — removes one more area where the management of what is seen has been required. The person who is partway through a Step 9 list often describes a feeling of accumulating lightness — not because the remaining amends are easier but because the person is less weighted than they were when they began. This is the progressive nature of what the amends produces. The first amends is the hardest. The fifth is easier than the first. The last is often the one that was feared most — and produces the most significant release. "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit." — Romans 8:1 KJV The position of Romans 8:1 — no condemnation — becomes more fully experienced as the amends list is worked. The doctrinal position was established in Step 5. The experiential reality of it develops through the action of Step 9. The person who completes the amends list carries less of the weight that has been mistaken for who they are. What remains is the person underneath — the one God made, the one the new life is producing.

THE ROAD FORWARD

The pattern across Scripture is that genuine encounter with God produces restitution — not because it is demanded, but because the person who has been genuinely changed cannot rest in the debt. Zacchaeus gave back fourfold before Jesus said a word about it.

Continue through the list. Do not stop between amends to process what the previous one produced. The processing happens best in the daily journal and with the mentor. The momentum of the list serves the student. Maintain it.

THE AMENDS THAT CHANGES THE RELATIONSHIP WITH SELF

Beyond the relationship with the harmed person, the amends changes the relationship the person has with themselves. The person who has never honestly accounted for a significant harm carries a version of the self that is smaller than the full truth — a managed version that cannot bear the full examination. The amends conversation, when made honestly, is the first time many people have stood fully in the truth of what they did and offered what they could without managing the presentation. That experience — of being the full self in the most honest possible conversation — is the beginning of a relationship with the self that does not require management. "And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." — John 8:32 KJV Jesus said this to people who had believed on Him — showing them what the truth that He embodied would do in the life that received it. The truth of the amends — the specific, honest, unmanaged truth offered directly to the person harmed — participates in the freedom that John 8:32 describes.

The person who has made honest amends is not the person who made the original harm. That person was governed by the bondage. This person is governed by something else — and the amends is the clearest possible evidence of the difference.

The relational ground cleared here does not need to be recultivated. Step 10 is the daily discipline that keeps what has been cleared from filling back in.

The amends to the self includes grieving what was lost.

The person who makes amends to everyone on the list but never addresses the harm done to their own life has left the most personal entry unaddressed. The addiction harmed you — not only the people around you. It took years, opportunities, the version of yourself that deserved to exist. That loss deserves to be named.

The amends to the self is not punishment. It is the honest acknowledgment of what was taken — and the decision, made concretely, to stop losing more of it.

"Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness." — Isaiah 61:3 KJV

The exchange is real. But the ashes must be named before the beauty can replace them. Grieve what was lost. Then choose, daily, to stop losing what remains.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 9 Lesson 2 MEMBER LESSON. This lesson addresses what the amends produces — primarily in the person making it. The surprise of the lifting is a significant pastoral moment. Name it clearly so students recognize it when it arrives. COVENANT CONTEXT FOR THE TEACHER Luke 19:9 — this day is salvation come to this house. The moment of Zacchaeus's announcement is also the moment Jesus speaks the result. The freedom does not wait for verification. It comes with the willing going. Help students se...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ James 5:16 KJV — "Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed."

ASSIGNMENT

Continue through the list 1. Make at least two more amends this week. 2. After each one write: what changed in me — not in the other person. 3. Bring your list progress to your mentor. How many completed. How many remaining. 4. Identify the amends you have been putting last. Schedule it now. Due: Before Lesson 3

quiz.question: According to James 5:16 KJV what does confessing faults one to another produce — and for whom?
choices: Forgiveness for the person who receives the confession — the amends benefits the person harmed
Healing for the person who makes the confession — the honest naming of what happened produces healing in the person who names it
Restoration of the relationship — both parties are healed equally by the act of confession

A record for accountability — the confession establishes what happened for future reference James 5:16 — confess your faults that ye may be healed. The healing described is for the person who confesses. The amends is not only an act of service toward the harmed person — it is the liberation of the person making it from the weight of the unaddressed harm.

lessons.title: First be reconciled to thy brother — Step 9 as the formation of a different kind of person
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
Paul wrote to the church at Corinth — born-again believers — about the ministry of reconciliation: "God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation." The person working through the amends list is not only addressing past harms. They are participating in the ministry that God committed to His people — the word of reconciliation carried from one person to another in the ordinary context of daily life. Step 9 is forming a different kind of person — not only completing a list.

Step 8 produced a list and a willingness. Step 9 is where willingness becomes action.

The amend is the evidence of the turn. Every person on the list represents a place where the old life reached into another life and left damage. The repentant person who has been genuinely changed does not leave that damage unaddressed. This is not penance — it is the natural direction of a life that has genuinely turned.

THE AMENDS AS CHARACTER FORMATION

The person who makes thirty amends over the course of Step 9 is not the same person who made the first one. The repeated experience of naming honestly, taking full responsibility, and offering to make things right — without defending, without referencing what was done to you, without managing the reception — produces a character that the self could not produce for itself. "And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope." — Romans 5:3-4 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Rome — describing the chain of character formation that difficulty produces in the person who does not avoid it. The amends conversations are difficult. They produce patience — the capacity to remain in an uncomfortable situation without exiting it. Patience produces experience — the accumulated knowledge of having done the difficult thing and survived it. Experience produces hope — not optimism but the settled assurance that the difficult thing can be faced because it has been faced before. The person who completes Step 9 honestly has a different relationship to the difficult conversation — with God, with others, with themselves. The pattern of honesty and accountability has been practiced enough to begin becoming the natural response rather than the effortful one.

The prodigal rehearsed his speech the whole way home. The father did not wait for the speech. He saw his son while he was yet a great way off and ran to meet him. The amends is not the performance — it is the arrival.

WHAT IS BEING FORMED

The character being formed in Step 9 is the character of the person who will work Step 12. The ambassador — the person who carries the word of reconciliation to others — must have walked the road they are inviting others to walk. The amends list is part of that road. Every conversation completed is the formation of the person who will one day sit across from someone at Step 1 and speak from the experience of having done it. "Now all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation." — 2 Corinthians 5:18 KJV The ministry of reconciliation is not a program. It is the overflow of a life that has been genuinely reconciled — to God and to the people the life has touched. Step 9 is where that reconciliation is worked out in the relational field with the same honesty and accountability that Steps 1-8 required internally.

THE ROAD FORWARD

The pattern across Scripture is that genuine encounter with God produces restitution — not because it is demanded, but because the person who has been genuinely changed cannot rest in the debt. Zacchaeus gave back fourfold before Jesus said a word about it.

The list is nearly complete. Lesson 4 closes the step and prepares the ground for Step 10 — the daily maintenance that carries what Step 9 built into the ongoing life. WHAT THE AMBASSADOR CARRIES "And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever." — John 14:16 KJV Jesus said this in the upper room — the night before the cross, to the people He was sending into the world. He was describing what He was about to send after He returned to the Father: not a temporary comfort but a permanent one. The Comforter who abides. Not the visit of the Spirit — the permanent dwelling of the Spirit. The person who completes Step 9 and carries the word of reconciliation to others in Step 12 carries this ministry — not from the self's capacity for compassion, not from the self's experience of recovery, but from the permanent indwelling of the Comforter who abides. The ambassador's resources are not the ambassador's own. They are the resources of the One who sent Him — the Comforter who does not depart when the conversation is difficult, who does not leave when the road is long, who abides. The ministry of reconciliation that Step 9 practices is the preparation for the ambassadorship of Step 12. And the ambassador who carries it carries more than their own story. They carry the Comforter who abides.

WHAT EQUIPPED THE MINISTRY OF RECONCILIATION

"But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth." — Acts 1:8 KJV Jesus said this just before He ascended — describing what would equip the disciples for the ministry of reconciliation that 2 Corinthians 5:18 commits to His people. Not their intelligence. Not their eloquence. Not even their genuine transformation, significant as that is. Power — after the Holy Ghost is come upon you. The ministry of reconciliation is not carried by people who have cleaned themselves up and become impressive. It is carried by people who have received power they did not manufacture — power that enables them to do what they could not do in their own capacity. The twelve steps of this curriculum are the road of preparation. The equipment for what the road leads to is what Acts 1:8 describes. Hold this question: what is the power that Jesus promised? And have you received it?

A STRONGER INHERITANCE — THE NAME THAT WAS GIVEN, NOT EARNED

Most people in recovery have spent significant energy trying to break what was inherited. Through effort. Through distance from the family. Through the determined decision to be different from what the pattern produced. Some of that distance helped. None of it reached the root. Because what is inherited at the level of the flesh cannot be broken by the will of the flesh. The will is part of what was inherited. The Scripture describes how Jesus received His name — not through achievement but through inheritance. "Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they." — Hebrews 1:4 KJV The name was not earned. It was inherited. The Father bestowed it. And the significance of this for everyone in this program is direct: the name that Jesus received by inheritance from the Father is the

name He places on His people in the covenant. "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins." — Matthew 1:21 KJV The name means Jehovah-Savior. The self-existent One, who appeared to Abraham as El Shaddai — God Almighty — and to Moses as Jehovah — I AM — revealed Himself fully and finally in the human Son: Jehovah manifest in flesh, bearing the name that contains every name that came before it. When Zechariah prophesied, "In that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one" — Zechariah 14:9 KJV — he was pointing to the moment when every compound name, every partial revelation, every aspect of God's character progressively disclosed across centuries, would be gathered into one name. That day came. The name is Jesus. And the person who receives that name through the covenant act enters a different inheritance than the one natural birth provided — not because they earned it, but because the One who inherited it first has made it available to those who enter through the door He opened.

DEBORAH — FAITHFULNESS OVER TIME PRODUCES AUTHORITY FOR THE MOMENT

Deborah judged Israel under a palm tree. She had not appointed herself. She had not campaigned for the position. The Scripture says the children of Israel came up to her for judgment — they came because she was the person God had formed, over time, in faithfulness. She was a mother in Israel. The authority was not seized. It was the natural product of a character formed through years of consistent, hidden faithfulness. "And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time." — Judges 4:4 KJV When the crisis came — when Barak needed to go to battle against Sisera and said he would not go unless Deborah went with him — she went. Not because she sought the position. Because the position was hers and the moment required it. She said to Barak: I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. The character that Step 9 is forming in the person who makes thirty amends is not preparation for a position they will seek. It is the development of the person who, when the moment of greatest need arrives in someone else's life, is ready. Deborah did not have an appointment. She was available because she had been faithful. The ambassador is not developed for the platform. They are developed for the person sitting at the side of the road.

The person who has made honest amends is not the person who made the original harm. That person was governed by the bondage. This person is governed by something else — and the amends is the clearest possible evidence of the difference.

The relational ground cleared here does not need to be recultivated. Step 10 is the daily discipline that keeps what has been cleared from filling back in.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 9 Lesson 3 MEMBER LESSON. This lesson reframes Step 9 from list completion to character formation. The student who is midway through the list often needs this perspective — the sense that the work is producing something beyond the individual conversations. COVENANT CONTEXT FOR THE TEACHER 2 Corinthians 5:18-19 — the ministry of reconciliation committed to the people of God. Step 9 is not private recovery work. It is practice in the ministry that God has committed to His people. Help stude...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ 2 Corinthians 5:18 KJV — "And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation."

ASSIGNMENT

Complete the list 1. Schedule and complete all remaining amends this week. 2. For each one write: what the amends produced in me — specifically in my character, not only in the relationship. 3. Identify how the person who is completing this list is different from the person who started it. Write one page. 4. Bring the completed list to your mentor for Step 9 closure. Due: Before Lesson 4

choices: Tribulation works weakness eventually producing dependence on God
Tribulation works patience patience works experience experience works hope — the difficult thing produces the settled character that hope describes
Tribulation works character refinement but only in proportion to the suffering endured

Tribulation is to be avoided where possible — patience is produced by rest not difficulty Romans 5:3-4 — tribulation worketh patience, patience worketh experience, experience worketh hope. The chain is specific: each difficulty met without exiting produces the next element. The person who completes Step 9 honestly has walked the full chain — and the hope at the end is not optimism but settled assurance.

lessons.title: The relational ground is cleared — completing Step 9 and what the road looks like after
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Jesus told the disciples to go into all the world and preach the gospel — the commission came after the resurrection, after the ministry, after the full work of the covenant had been accomplished. The going that Step 12 will describe is not the going of an unformed person who has decided to help others. It is the going of a person whose life has been changed by the road they have walked. Step 9 is a significant portion of that road — and its completion marks a moment worth standing in honestly before moving forward.

Step 8 produced a list and a willingness. Step 9 is where willingness becomes action.

The amend is the evidence of the turn. Every person on the list represents a place where the old life reached into another life and left damage. The repentant person who has been genuinely changed does not leave that damage unaddressed. This is not penance — it is the natural direction of a life that has genuinely turned.

THE RELATIONAL GROUND IS CLEARED

The list is done. Every amends honestly prepared in Step 8 has been honestly offered in Step 9. Not every relationship has been restored — the reception of the amends belongs to the other person. But the offering has been made. What was owed has been addressed. The relational ground is cleared. "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." — Romans 5:1 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Rome — describing the peace that the justified position produces. The peace with God described in Romans 5:1 has a relational analog in what Step 9 produces — not the restoration of every relationship but the clearing of what the person carried into every relationship. The person who completes Step 9 honestly stands in a different relational field than the person who began it.

WHAT STEP 9 LEAVES BEHIND

The prodigal rehearsed his speech the whole way home. The father did not wait for the speech. He saw his son while he was yet a great way off and ran to meet him. The amends is not the performance — it is the arrival.

The list leaves behind a record of a person who went. Who named what happened. Who took responsibility. Who offered to make it right. The reception was not always what was hoped. Some relationships were restored. Some were not. But the going happened — and the person who went is not the same person who drew up the list.

WHAT STEP 9 OPENED

Step 10 opens a life of daily examination — the maintenance of what Step 9 cleared. The person who has cleared the relational ground is positioned to keep it clear through the daily inventory of Step 10. Without Step 9, Step 10 is maintenance of a field that has not been cleared. After Step 9, Step 10 is the daily keeping of what the amends opened. Step 11 opens the deepening of the relationship with God — the drawing nigh that produces the drawing nigh of God toward you. The person who has cleared the relational field with others through Steps 8 and 9 brings that same cleared posture to the relationship with God in Step 11.

THE ROAD FORWARD

The pattern across Scripture is that genuine encounter with God produces restitution — not because it is demanded, but because the person who has been genuinely changed cannot rest in the debt. Zacchaeus gave back fourfold before Jesus said a word about it.

Step 9 is complete. The road continues. Step 10 begins immediately — not as a new burden but as the daily practice that maintains what has been built.

THE LIVING AMENDS CONTINUES

For the amends that could not be made through direct conversation — the deceased, the unreachable, the person where contact would cause harm — the living amends is not a substitute that is completed in Step 9 and then finished. It is the ongoing way of life in the specific area where the harm occurred. The person who stole from their employer makes the living amends by becoming a person of complete financial integrity in the ongoing life. The person who was dishonest with a parent who has since died makes the living amends by becoming a person who tells the truth in the ongoing life. The living amends has no completion date. It is the permanent testimony of the changed life.

"Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven." — Matthew 5:16 KJV The light of the changed life is the ongoing amends — not only to the people on the list but to everyone whose life touches the person's. The living amends is visible. It speaks. And it points toward the One who made it possible.

The person who has made honest amends is not the person who made the original harm. That person was governed by the bondage. This person is governed by something else — and the amends is the clearest possible evidence of the difference.

The relational ground cleared here does not need to be recultivated. Step 10 is the daily discipline that keeps what has been cleared from filling back in.

TEACHER NOTES

Its function is honest closure — naming what was accomplished, what was not accomplished, and what the completion opened for the steps that follow. COVENANT CONTEXT FOR THE TEACHER Romans 5:1 — justified by faith, peace with God. The peace described here has an analog in what Step 9 produces relationally. lessons.title: Let a man examine himself — continued personal inventory and the promptly principle
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When Nehemiah rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem, the workers carried their tools in one hand and their weapons in the other — building and watching simultaneously. The work of construction and the work of vigilance happened at the same time, not in sequence. Step 10 is the posture of Nehemiah's workers — the daily examination is not a return to Step 4 as though the earlier work failed. It is the ongoing vigilance of a person who has cleared the ground and intends to keep it clear.

Step 9 cleared the ground of the past. Step 10 is the daily practice that keeps it clear.

The God before whom the daily examination takes place is one Spirit, one LORD — who knows the heart before the examination begins and is not surprised by what the inventory finds.

The daily inventory of Step 10 is the practice of a person who has understood what name they are living under. Every day, the question the inventory asks is the same: did I live today under the name that has been placed on me, or under the old names the flesh still reaches for? The answer shapes the next day's starting point.

Daily inventory is daily repentance made practical. The person who takes a daily inventory and promptly admits when wrong is practicing what Paul the apostle described as dying daily — the ongoing posture of a life that continues to turn toward God rather than toward self.

LET A MAN EXAMINE HIMSELF

"But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup." — 1 Corinthians 11:28 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers at Corinth — instructing them in the self-examination that the participation in the Lord's table requires. The examination is not annual. It is not occasional. It is the posture that accompanies each participation — the daily return to honest self-assessment before bringing what is there before God. Step 10 applies this same discipline to the daily life: examine yourself today. Not the accumulated inventory of years — that was Step 4. Today's inventory. The resentment that formed this morning. The fear that drove the decision this afternoon. The harm that was caused in the conversation this evening. Examine it today, while it is today.

Paul the apostle wrote about dying daily — not from a position of arrival, but from the ongoing practice of a person who knew that the flesh does not retire. The daily examination is not evidence of failure. It is the practice of the person who has understood.

THE PROMPTLY PRINCIPLE

"Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin." — James 4:17 KJV The sin of omission — the known thing not done, the wrong not addressed, the amends not promptly made — is identified by James as sin in the same way the sin of commission is. The promptly principle of Step 10 is the application of James 4:17 to the daily life: when you find you are wrong today, say so today. Do not accumulate a new inventory. Address it at the inventory's smallest unit.

WHY PROMPTLY MATTERS

The resentment held overnight is harder to address in the morning. The wrong not addressed this week is harder to acknowledge next week. The pattern of delay is the same pattern Step 4 revealed — the management of what is seen, the protection of the position, the avoidance of the uncomfortable honest conversation.

Promptly is not only a discipline for the relationship with the harmed person. It is the practice that prevents the daily inventory from becoming the accumulated inventory that Step 4 required. The person who addresses today's wrongs today has no week-long backlog to manage. The person who defers accumulates a Step 4 that keeps growing.

WHAT THE DAILY EXAMINATION INCLUDES

Today's resentment — anything from today's interactions that produced the familiar feeling of re-living a wound. Name it. Was it justified? What did I do with it? Today's fear — what drove a decision that the honest examination shows was fear-based. Name it. What would the faith-based decision have looked like? Today's harm — any person who, as a result of today's interactions, now has something against me. Name them. What is owed? Today's omission — what I knew to do today and did not do. Name it.

THE FOUR WARNING STATES — HALT

Recovery communities use four words as a daily self-assessment: Hungry. Angry. Lonely. Tired. Each of these states has been shown to reliably precede a return to use — not because they cause the return directly, but because each one drops the guard that the daily examination is designed to keep in place.

Hungry — the neglected body is the vulnerable body. The person who has not eaten is operating on less than what the spiritual and relational work of recovery requires.

Angry — the resentment not addressed by end of day is harder to address tomorrow. The fourth column of Step 4 showed where anger lives. The daily examination asks whether it returned today.

Lonely — isolation was the companion of the bondage. The person who is drifting back toward isolation is drifting back toward the conditions that produced the pattern. The daily examination asks: who did I contact today? Who contacted me?

Tired — exhaustion drops every guard. The daily examination includes: am I getting sleep? Is the body being treated as the vessel it is?

Add to the daily examination a fifth question: which of these four is active right now? And what is the honest response to it?

THE CRAVING LOG

When a craving arrives, write it down the same day. Four things: What was I doing before it came? What was I feeling before it came? What did I do when it arrived? How long did it last?

The craving log turns an internal shame event into information. Reviewed with the mentor, it reveals patterns that the examination alone cannot see. The person who tracks their cravings is the person who begins to understand them — and the person who understands them is the person who is no longer surprised by them.

NEHEMIAH — BUILDING THE WALL WITH A SWORD IN ONE HAND

Nehemiah was not a prophet or a priest. He was a cupbearer to a pagan king — a position that required absolute trustworthiness, constant attention, and the kind of daily faithfulness that kept the king alive.

When the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and the people were in reproach, Nehemiah asked the king for permission to go and rebuild. He was granted it. And when he arrived and began the work, the enemies of the project arose immediately — Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, the Ashdodites — surrounding the builders and threatening to stop the work.

Nehemiah's response is the description of Step 10 in practice: "Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night." — Nehemiah 4:9 KJV

And then: "They which builded on the wall, and they that bare burdens, with those that laded, every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon." — Nehemiah 4:17 KJV

One hand building. One hand holding the weapon. The work and the watchfulness at the same time — simultaneously, without separating them into different seasons.

Step 10 is built on this image. The person who maintains a daily inventory is not stopping the building to do the watching, or stopping the watching to do the building. They are doing both at the same time — making the daily progress that recovery requires while maintaining the daily vigilance that keeps the ground already gained from being lost.

The name Nehemiah means the LORD comforts. He did his work in a city of reproach, surrounded by enemies, with a trowel in one hand and a sword in the other. And the wall was finished in fifty-two days.

The examination continues. The building continues. Both at once. That is Step 10.

THE ROAD FORWARD

This is the pattern Paul the apostle described as dying daily — not a single event, but a practice. The ongoing inventory is not the evidence of a person who has not arrived. It is the practice of a person who understands that the flesh does not retire, and has stopped pretending otherwise.

Step 10 is not a step — it is a daily life. It does not complete. It continues into Step 11 and Step 12 as the permanent discipline of the person who has cleared the ground and intends to keep it clear. Lesson 2 gives the four areas of daily inventory in practical detail. Begin the daily examination tonight.

THE EXAMINATION INCLUDES THIS QUESTION

"But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his." — Romans 8:9 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Rome — giving them the mark by which the honest examination can assess its own standing. Not church attendance. Not moral improvement. Not the length of the recovery. The Spirit of God dwelling within. Step 10 is the step of continued self-examination. The examination is honest and it does not exclude this question. The daily inventory of Step 10 keeps the ground clear — and the cleared ground is precisely what makes it possible to honestly ask: does the Spirit of God dwell in me? Not as a doctrine I affirm. As a present reality I have received. The curriculum has been building toward this question since the first lesson. The honest answer to it — whatever the honest answer is — is the most important entry in any inventory.

The person who maintains a daily inventory is not performing accountability — they are living as someone for whom honesty has become the default. That is transformation at the level of character, not behavior. That is what the steps have been building.

The examined life and the prayerful life are the two disciplines that sustain everything the prior steps built. Step 11 is where the examined life finds its source.

The daily examination Paul the apostle described in 1 Corinthians 15:31 — dying daily — is the same pattern Acts records in the life of every person who received the Spirit. The Spirit who entered does not leave the person to maintain the life through willpower. He sustains. But the daily examination keeps the channel clear.

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ James 4:17 KJV — "Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin."

ASSIGNMENT

Begin the daily examination 1. Tonight before sleep: examine the four areas — resentment, fear, harm, omission. Write what surfaces in each. 2. Address promptly anything from today that can be addressed before the day ends. 3. Do this every night this week. Bring the week's record to your mentor. 4. Identify which area shows up most frequently. What does the pattern show? Due: Before Lesson 2

quiz.question: According to 1 Corinthians 11:28 KJV what should a man do before participating — and how does this become the model for the daily inventory of Step 10?
choices: Pray for the community — the examination is collective not individual
Examine himself — the same posture of honest self-assessment before significant participation becomes the daily discipline of Step 10 applied to every day not only to formal observance
Confess publicly — the examination requires group witness to be valid

Receive permission from a spiritual authority — the examination alone is insufficient 1 Corinthians 11:28 — let a man examine himself. Paul wrote this to born-again believers — the self-examination that precedes the Lord's table is the model for the daily examination of Step 10. Applied daily, it prevents the accumulation that Step 4 had to address annually.
