lessons.title: Commissioned by the Author of eternal salvation — establishing what is real before you go
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
Commissioned by the Author of eternal salvation — establishing what is real before you go ■ MEMBER — Login Required

In Step 1 we admitted we were powerless. What we carry now is the evidence that powerlessness was not the end of the story.

The God who sends the ambassador is one Spirit, one LORD — and the testimony the ambassador carries is not a testimony about a concept. It is a testimony about a person encountered, a name received, a life genuinely changed.

MEMBER LESSON

The examination of Lesson 1 revealed what is actually there. Lesson 2 addresses what to do with what is real — how to strengthen it, structure it, and make it stable under the conditions that will test it. Peter wrote this instruction to people already called and elected — addressing not how to enter that standing but how to make it sure in the daily walk of those who had already entered: "Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall." — 2 Peter 1:10 KJV Give diligence to make it sure. Not assume it is sure because the year was completed. Give diligence — the active, sustained, intentional work of establishing what the examination confirmed. The calling and the election are real. The diligence makes them sure in the daily lived experience. What is real must be built. What is built must be maintained. What is maintained becomes stable. And stability under pressure is what the commissioned life requires before it can carry anything to anyone else.

The disciples were in a locked room when the risen Christ appeared. Not on a mountaintop. Not in the temple. In a locked room, afraid. He came through the walls. The commission came before the fear was gone.

THE FOUNDATION THAT HOLDS

"Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock." — Matthew 7:24-25 KJV The rain came. The flood came. The wind came. Not because the builder made a mistake — because that is the condition of life. The question is not whether the storms arrive but what the house is built on when they do. The foundation established in Step 12 is not the twelve-step program. It is the Word — heard and done. The daily reading that is not optional. The prayer that is not occasional. The obedience that is not selective. These are not spiritual extras for the advanced. They are the foundation that determines whether what was built survives the conditions that are coming. The person who completes twelve steps and reduces the daily disciplines — who treats the Word as something they got enough of in the program — is building on sand without knowing it. The flood reveals the foundation. Build it before the flood, not after.

ELIMINATING DOUBLE-MINDEDNESS

"A double minded man is unstable in all his ways." — James 1:8 KJV Double-mindedness is the specific enemy of the established life. Not dramatic failure — the subtle maintenance of two positions. The surrender that was genuine in the room and qualified when alone. The faith that declares

God's provision on Sunday and worries about money on Monday. The commitment to the daily disciplines that holds when life is manageable and dissolves under pressure. Eliminating double-mindedness is the work of Step 12 establishment. Not through greater willpower — through the clarity of what the examination confirmed and the decision to build on that exclusively. The double-minded person is trying to build two houses simultaneously. Establishment requires choosing one foundation and building there completely. What other masters are still being served? Name them. The double-mindedness lives in the named thing that has not yet been released.

BUILDING CONSISTENCY UNDER PRESSURE

The established life is not built in comfortable conditions. It is built in the ordinary pressure of the life the person returns to — the workplace, the family, the financial reality, the relationships that do not automatically improve because the program was completed. "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the LORD your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you." — Deuteronomy 31:6 KJV God goes with — into the pressure, not around it. The establishment of Step 12 is the building of the life that holds in the pressure because it is built on what does not move. The God who goes with does not remove the conditions. He establishes the person within them. Consistency is built repetition by repetition. The morning that was given to God even when the day demanded it from the first moment. The amends maintained even when the person receiving it has not changed. The daily inventory kept even when nothing dramatic surfaced. Each repetition is a brick. The building becomes what it is through the accumulated bricks of ordinary consistency.

ALIGNING ACTIONS WITH BELIEF

The final test of establishment is alignment — whether what the person says they believe matches what their daily actions declare they believe. "For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also." — James 2:26 KJV Dead faith is the faith that declares but does not act. The person who believes in the daily Word but does not read it. The person who believes in the power of prayer but does not pray. The person who believes God can restore what was damaged but has not taken the Step 9 action that the restoration requires. Establishment means the belief and the action are the same thing. Not in alignment eventually. Now. The action declares the belief more loudly than the declaration does. What your Monday morning looks like is the evidence of what you actually believe — more accurate than anything said in a meeting. The commissioned life is built on established faith — examined, confirmed real, and structured into the daily action that declares it true. THE NAME IN FULLNESS — THE FAMILY IDENTIFIED "For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named." — Ephesians 3:14-15 KJV

Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Ephesus — identifying the family of God by the name that governs it. The whole family — in heaven and on earth — is named. Not self-named. Named by the Father whose family it is. The covenant pattern was planted early in this curriculum: God places His name upon His people. Numbers 6:27 — they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them. The Old Testament priests placed the Name upon the people in blessing. What the Old Testament established as pattern, the New Testament completes as reality. "Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord." — Acts 22:16 KJV This is the moment the Name is placed — not as a label but as a family identification, not as a ceremony but as the covenant act by which the person enters the family in heaven and on earth that Ephesians 3:15 describes. The surname of God placed upon the person by God's own instruction, in the water, in the name above every name. "There is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved." — Acts 4:12 KJV One name. Not a title — a name. The name that was placed upon Israel in the blessing. The name that God told Moses to put upon the children of Israel. The name that the whole family in heaven and earth bears. The name that must be called upon to receive the promise of Acts 2:38-39. Jesus. That is the name. And the ambassador who carries the word of reconciliation carries it under that name — and to that name — and in that name — in every word and deed, in every conversation, in every life that the road of the twelve steps leads them to.

They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. That is the pattern of Step 12. Not by performance. Not by perfection. By what God has done, and the honest account of it.

THE NAME THE AMBASSADOR CARRIES

The ambassador does not carry a concept. They carry a name.

Revelation 22:4 KJV records the final state of those who have walked the full road: "And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads." The name is upon them — not a generic identity, but a specific name. The same name that was placed upon them in baptism. The same name that has governed the life across twelve steps.

Ephesians 3:14-15 KJV: "Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named." God has a family. That family bears His name. The family name of God — the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost — is not a category. It is a specific name. Jesus. And the family bears it.

The ambassador of Step 12 carries this name into the field. Not as a slogan. Not as a denominational label. As an identity — the identity of a person who has been surnamed by God, who has called on His name, who has been baptized in that name, who has received the Spirit that comes in that name, and who now carries that name into every relationship and every room they enter.

Acts 4:12 KJV: "Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved."

The ambassador knows the name. They have been changed by what that name does. And they carry the testimony of a person who has received what the name promised — not as a theory, but as an experience.

The word of their testimony (Rev 12:11 KJV) is not a story about religion. It is a story about a name placed on a person who was not looking for it — and what happened when it was received.

THE HOUSEHOLD OF THE AMBASSADOR

The people who lived through the unchanged life are the first field of Step 12.

The spouse who stayed — or who left and may be willing to hear a word from a different person than the one they left. The children who watched and learned and formed their understanding of what love looks like from what the addiction modeled. The parents who prayed. The sibling who covered for you longer than was good for them.

These are not the distant mission field. These are the people whose Step 12 begins before any stranger has been reached.

"And as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD." — Joshua 24:15 KJV

Joshua made this declaration at the end of the journey — after the wilderness, after the battles, after the long road from Egypt to Canaan. He did not make it in the middle of the bondage. He made it after the road had changed him enough to say it honestly.

The changed life that Step 12 carries is most visible to the people who know the unchanged life. They are the hardest audience and the most important one. The testimony that reaches them — slowly, through consistency, through the living amends that continues long after the formal amends conversation — is the most powerful testimony the ambassador carries.

Three questions for the household: What does the person I am now owe the people who lived through the person I was? Which relationships from the old life are available to be rebuilt — and what does rebuilding require? What does it look like for this household to be governed differently than it was?

The ambassador does not only go out. They come home. And the home is the first place the mission is proven real.

DELIVERED FROM — AND DELIVERED FOR

There is a statement this curriculum saves for this lesson because it belongs here, at the point where the ambassador understands the full scope of what has happened to them: You were not just delivered from something. You were delivered for something. The deliverance from the addiction, the bondage, the patterns of the flesh — that deliverance was real and it was costly and it is not minimized here. But the person who defines their entire testimony by what they were delivered from has only told half the story. The first half. The essential half. But half. "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound." — Isaiah 61:1 KJV Jesus read this passage in the synagogue in Nazareth and sat down and said: this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears. He was describing not only what He had come to do — but what the people He delivered through that work would be commissioned to do. The captive set free becomes the one who carries liberty to the next captive. The one whose prison opened becomes the one who opens another prison door by their testimony and their presence in the field. The Israel that came out of Egypt did not come out to wander. The deliverance had a destination. The Israelites who accepted the wilderness as the final answer to Egypt never reached the land. The person who accepts deliverance from the addiction as the final answer has stopped at the right place but not yet reached the

destination. You were delivered from something. Name it. Honor the weight of it. And then turn and face what you were delivered for — because the God who paid the price to get you out of Egypt did not do it so you could make a life in the wilderness.

The person who has walked all twelve steps honestly is not the person who arrived at Step 1. That is not an exaggeration — it is the testimony Scripture promises to those who walk the road faithfully. They overcame. Not they tried to overcome. They overcame.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 12 Lesson 2 — Establishment MEMBER LESSON. The movement from Lesson 1 (examination) to Lesson 2 (establishment) assumes the examination produced honest results. Before this session begins — ask: did anything surface in the examination that needs to be addressed before establishment work begins? The person who identified hidden compromise in Lesson 1 needs to bring that to God and the mentor before building on what was compromised. 2 PETER 1:10 — MAKE YOUR CALLING SURE: The diligence here is...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ 2 Peter 1:10 KJV — "Give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall."

■ Matthew 7:24 KJV — "Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock."

■ James 1:8 KJV — "A double minded man is unstable in all his ways."

ASSIGNMENT

Establishment — building what the examination confirmed 1. Audit one full week: write what your daily schedule actually declared you believe — not what you said but what the time showed. Morning given to God or phone? First financial decision — first fruits or remainder? 2. Name the double-mindedness. Where are you building two houses? What other master is receiving what belongs to God? 3. Build a...

quiz.question: According to 2 Peter 1:10 KJV what must the person give diligence to — and what does diligence produce?
choices: Give diligence to helping others — and produce a legacy of discipleship
Give diligence to make your calling and election sure — producing the stability that means you shall never fall
Give diligence to theological study — producing the knowledge that supports the commission

Give diligence to outreach — producing the multiplication Step 12 requires 2 Peter 1:10 — give diligence to make your calling and election sure, for if ye do these things ye shall never fall. The calling and election are real — the diligence makes them sure in the daily lived experience. Not assuming — building. The stability that shall never fall is built, not given.

quiz.question: According to Matthew 7:24-25 KJV what is the difference between the wise man and the foolish man — and when is the difference revealed?
choices: The wise man had better circumstances — the difference was revealed in what God gave each
The wise man heard the word — the foolish man did not, and the difference was immediate
The wise man heard and did — the foolish man heard without doing, and the difference was revealed when the storm came

The wise man had more faith — the difference was revealed in the size of the results Matthew 7:24-25 — the wise man heard and did. The foolish man heard without doing. Both houses looked the same — until the rain, flood, and wind came. The storm reveals the foundation. The question is not whether the storm comes but what was built before it arrived.

quiz.question: According to James 2:26 KJV what does the alignment of faith and works reveal — and what does the absence of works indicate?
choices: Works reveal spiritual maturity — their absence indicates early stage faith that will grow
As the body without the spirit is dead — so faith without works is dead. Works are the evidence that the faith is alive
Works reveal commitment level — their absence indicates insufficient motivation rather than dead faith

Works are the goal of faith — their presence indicates successful completion of the program James 2:26 — as the body without the spirit is dead so faith without works is dead also. The establishment test: do the actions align with the belief? What the Monday morning schedule declares is more accurate evidence of actual belief than anything said in a meeting.

lessons.title: When the glory fills the house — the equipment the ambassador actually carries
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
When the glory fills the house — the equipment the ambassador actually carries ■ MEMBER — Login Required

In Step 1 we admitted we were powerless. What we carry now is the evidence that powerlessness was not the end of the story.

MEMBER LESSON

Step 12 — Commissioned Living: Examine, Establish, and Lead. The eleven steps that preceded this one were not the source of the transformation — they were the road of obedience through which God worked. What God did in that obedience has cleared what needed to be cleared and built what needed to be built. The vessel is available. And what God fills the available vessel with is the equipment the commission requires. The disciples who carried the message that changed the world were not carrying program completion. They were carrying what had happened to them in that upper room. "And tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high." — Luke 24:49 KJV Endued. Clothed. Equipped. The ambassador does not go in his own clothing. He wears what was given from above. The commission without the enduing is premature — and the field can tell the difference between the overflow of a filled life and the effort of an empty one.

WHEN THE GLORY FILLS THE HOUSE — 2 CHRONICLES 7:1-2

The disciples were in a locked room when the risen Christ appeared. Not on a mountaintop. Not in the temple. In a locked room, afraid. He came through the walls. The commission came before the fear was gone.

The picture of what happened at Pentecost was drawn a thousand years before it occurred. "Now when Solomon had made an end of praying, the fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of the LORD filled the house. And the priests could not

enter into the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD's house." — 2 Chronicles 7:1-2 KJV One hundred and twenty priests. All in their appointed places. All doing what priests do — their instruments ready, their robes on, their functions assigned. The sacrifice had been offered. The prayer had been prayed. The preparation was complete. And when the glory of the LORD filled the house they could not stand to minister. Not because they were unprepared. Because what arrived exceeded what any prepared flesh could remain upright in. The flesh has a ceiling. The glory of God has no ceiling. When the two meet — when the fully surrendered, fully prepared vessel encounters the fullness of God — what happens is beyond what the flesh can produce, explain, or contain. This is the picture of Pentecost.

AND SUDDENLY — ACTS 2:1-4

"And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost." — Acts 2:1-4 KJV Wind. Fire. Filled. All the house. Each of them. The same elements Solomon's priests experienced — fire from heaven, the glory filling the house, the flesh unable to stand in it. The same God. The same pattern. The flesh positioned in one accord, the sacrifice of self-will offered through the obedience of ten steps, the prayer sustained through Step 11 — and when the day of Pentecost was fully come, suddenly. Suddenly is God's timing, not the person's. The one accord is the person's posture. The suddenly belongs to God. The one who has been in the posture of Acts 1:14 — continuing with one accord in prayer — receives the suddenly when God determines the vessel is ready.

THESE MEN ARE NOT DRUNK — ACTS 2:13-14

"Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice." — Acts 2:13-14 KJV The flesh watching what happened at Pentecost had one explanation: new wine. Intoxication. Something chemical that produced the behavior they were observing. They were not wrong about the appearance. They were completely wrong about the source. The Spirit-filled life is not explainable by the flesh observing it. It does not compute. The joy is real but it is not manufactured. The boldness is present but it is not produced by training. The love is unmistakable but it is not sustained by effort. The fruit of the Spirit in the genuinely filled life looks — to the uninitiated flesh — exactly like something the flesh knows how to do but better. It takes the form the flesh understands and fills it with something the flesh cannot produce.

The person who has been genuinely filled carries something the field recognizes as different without always being able to name what is different. Acts 4:13 names it: they took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The encounter is evident in the carrier. The field can tell. Peter did not argue with the mocking. He stood up, lifted his voice, and gave the testimony of what God had done — and then the commission.

THE GREAT COMMISSION — ACTS 2:38

"Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost." — Acts 2:38 KJV This is the commission Peter carried into the field — not as a program description but as the message of what God was offering to everyone who heard. Repent — the genuine turning away from sin and toward God. Not the feeling of sorrow. The actual turning of the will. What the steps have been practicing as a discipline — the daily surrender, the continued giving over — points toward this: the decision of a person who turns fully and does not look back. Baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ — not the titles Father, Son, and Holy Ghost as three separate names but the one name into which those titles resolve. Matthew 28:19 says baptize in the name — singular. Acts 2:38 reveals that name. Jesus Christ. This is the obedience of water baptism, in the name, as God commanded. For the remission of sins — the account settled. Not managed. Not reduced. Remitted — sent away, cancelled, the record cleared. This is what the blood of Christ accomplished, applied through the obedience of repentance and baptism. And ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost — the promise of the Father. What Luke 24:49 called power from on high. What 2 Chronicles 7 pictured when fire fell and the glory filled the house. The gift given to the obedient — not assumed for every person who hears the message, but promised to every person who obeys it. The ambassador carries this message. The Step 12 person knows what the commission says. They carry it to the field — not as a declaration of what has already happened to the person they are speaking to, but as the offer of what God promises to the person who will obey. THE AMBASSADOR'S EQUIPMENT — LUKE 24:49 / ACTS 4:13

The disciples who went into the world after Pentecost were not carrying the same thing they were carrying before the upper room. Before the upper room they had three years with Jesus, the resurrection appearances, the commission itself — and they were told not to go yet. After the upper room they had the same things — and the promise of the Father filling every cleared vessel that had positioned in one accord. The difference was not theology. It was equipment. "Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus." — Acts 4:13 KJV

Unlearned. Ignorant by the world's standard. No credentials that the Sanhedrin recognized. And they could not answer the boldness or the works. The equipment the ambassador carries is not accumulated through program completion. It is given through the filling. The cleared vessel, filled with the Holy Ghost, carries what the eleven steps of preparation made room for — and what the field recognizes as the thing they cannot explain and cannot dismiss.

STANDING IN THE GAP BEFORE GOING

Before the ambassador arrives at the conversation — the ambassador has been in the presence. Not the presence of a meeting. The presence of God. "And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none." — Ezekiel 22:30 KJV God sought for a person who would stand in the gap. The ambassador of Step 12 is that person — standing in the gap for the specific person in the field before the conversation happens. Praying specifically. Naming them. Asking God to prepare the ground before the foot arrives. Paul described this intercession to born-again believers who had received the Spirit — the Spirit making intercession is the operation of the indwelling Spirit already present in the obedient life: "Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered." — Romans 8:26 KJV The Spirit intercedes through the person who has been filled — for the person who is not yet saved, in language that exceeds what the filled person can articulate. The ambassador who prays before going arrives at a conversation that has already been prepared. The intercession model: name the person, pray specifically for them by name daily for one week before approaching. Watch what God does in the conversation that follows. The ambassador does not arrive alone. The Spirit has been there first.

THE PROMISE UNTO YOU

"For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call." — Acts 2:39 KJV The person in Step 12 who has received the gift of the Holy Ghost carries this promise into the field. Not as theology to argue. As testimony to offer. The promise is unto you — the specific person in front of me — and to your children, and to all that are afar off.

THE ACTS 19 PATTERN — WHAT THE AMBASSADOR DOES

"He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed?" — Acts 19:2 KJV Paul's first question to the sincere disciples at Ephesus was the question of the threshold. Not: do you believe? They believed. Not: are you repentant? They had repented. The question was whether what God had promised had been received. And when they said they had not heard whether there was a Holy Ghost — Paul met them where they were, affirmed what was genuine, and led them forward into what was still available.

This is the model for the ambassador of Step 12. Not the confrontation that accuses. Not the indifference that leaves people incomplete. The loving, informed, patient leading of sincere people toward the fullness of what God has promised — beginning where they are, honoring what is genuine, and walking forward together. The person who has received the promise — who has been through the threshold, has heard the sound, has received the witness — carries something that cannot be manufactured by any program, any effort, or any sincerity of intention. They carry the testimony of Acts 2:39: the promise is unto you and to your children and to all that are afar off. The ambassador's task is to carry that testimony — faithfully, lovingly, without coercion — to every person God sends across their path. The field the ambassador enters is full of people for whom the promise is already written. They do not know the promise exists. They do not know the door is open. They do not know that the God who filled the upper room is still filling cleared vessels that position in one accord and ask. The ambassador knows. And the knowing is the message.

Scripture shows two distinct realities that must not be collapsed. The first is the moment the Spirit enters the believer — the New Birth, the point of indwelling, what Acts records consistently from the upper room to Ephesus. The second is the ongoing operations of the Spirit through the believer — what Paul the apostle describes in First Corinthians 12 as the diversities of gifts distributed as the Spirit wills.

These are not the same category. Entry precedes operation. The Spirit enters the believer first. The Spirit then operates through the believer in varied gifts for the building of the body. Confusing these two collapses the order that both Acts and Paul keep carefully distinct.

The question is not which gifts a person might receive. The question is whether the Spirit has entered — and Scripture shows consistently what that entrance sounds like when it comes.

PRACTICING THESE PRINCIPLES IN ALL YOUR AFFAIRS

"And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him." — Colossians 3:17 KJV Practicing the principles in all your affairs is the final phrase of the program — and the one that extends furthest beyond it. Not in the meeting. Not in the Step 12 conversation. In all your affairs — the workplace, the home, the finances, the relationship that tests patience, the moment no one from the program is watching. The principle practiced in all affairs is the evidence that it has moved from lesson content to lived reality. Not what the person says they believe — what the Monday morning schedule, the financial decision, the conflict at home, and the private moment declare.

They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. That is the pattern of Step 12. Not by performance. Not by perfection. By what God has done, and the honest account of it.

THE NAME AS EQUIPMENT — WHAT THE AMBASSADOR ACTUALLY CARRIES

Every ambassador is sent with something. The ambassador of Step 12 carries more than a story of recovery. They carry the name that makes what they experienced possible for others.

The equipment is specific. Acts 2:38 is not merely a historical record. It is the standing instruction — the same instruction Peter gave on the day the church began, the same instruction that has produced the same result in every generation since. Repentance. Baptism in Jesus name for remission of sins. The gift of the Holy Ghost. This is the complete equipment of the New Testament ambassador.

The person in Step 12 who has received this fully carries something others do not have. They carry the testimony of someone who has walked the road of preparation — the honest admission of Step 1, the daily surrender of Step 3, the inventory of Step 4, the confession of Step 5, the readiness of Step 6, the humble request of Step 7, the amends of Steps 8 and 9, the daily maintenance of Step 10, the prayer and contact of Step 11 — and arrived at the threshold where the full covenant response was received.

That is the testimony Rev 12:11 KJV describes: "And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony." Not by performance. Not by perfection. By what God did — in a name — in a person who was willing to receive it.

The ambassador does not manufacture this testimony. They carry it because they walked the road honestly and received what was at the end of the road. That is what Step 12 sends into the field.

"And all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord." — Deuteronomy 28:10 KJV

The name is visible. It distinguishes the person who carries it. Not in the sense of religious performance — in the sense of a life that works differently than it did before the name was placed on it.

That is the equipment. That is the ambassador. That is Step 12.

ANANIAS OF DAMASCUS — SENT TOWARD WHAT FRIGHTENED HIM

"And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord. And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth." — Acts 9:10-11 KJV Ananias knew who Saul was. The name was not obscure. The man who had authority to arrest and imprison everyone who called on the name of Jesus — that man was the assignment. And Ananias said: Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints. He named the fear honestly. He did not pretend it was not there. He told God exactly what he knew and why the assignment seemed unreasonable. And the Lord said: go thy way, for he is a chosen vessel unto me. Ananias went. He laid his hands on the man who had come to Damascus to arrest believers and said: Brother Saul. Not enemy Saul. Brother. And in that moment — the moment of obedience that overrode what was reasonable from Ananias's position — the man who would become Paul received his sight and was filled with the Holy Ghost. The ambassador of Step 12 will be sent toward people who frighten them. Former associates. People who remind them of the worst of the old life. People in situations they recognize and have reasons to avoid. The Ananias

assignment is the test of whether the deliverance has been received deeply enough to produce that kind of obedience. Not fearless obedience — Ananias named the fear. Obedience that goes anyway.

The person who has walked all twelve steps honestly is not the person who arrived at Step 1. That is not an exaggeration — it is the testimony Scripture promises to those who walk the road faithfully. They overcame. Not they tried to overcome. They overcame.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 12 Lesson 3 — When the Glory Fills the House MEMBER LESSON. This is the theological center of the entire curriculum — where the journey of twelve steps connects to the power that makes the Step 12 commission possible. Do not rush it. Give it the full session. 2 CHRONICLES 7:1-2 — THE TEMPLE: Read this passage slowly. Let the picture land. One hundred and twenty priests — prepared, positioned, doing what priests do. And the glory of the LORD filled the house and they could not stand to minis...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ 2 Chronicles 7:1 KJV — "The fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of the LORD filled the house."

■ Acts 2:4 KJV — "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost."

■ Acts 2:38 KJV — "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost."

■ Acts 2:39 KJV — "For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off."

■ Ezekiel 22:30 KJV — "I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land."

ASSIGNMENT

The equipment and the intercession 1. Read Acts 2:1-39 in full. Write: what did Peter carry into that conversation that made it different from anything he had said before Pentecost? What was the specific difference? 2. Name one specific person who is in the field — who is where you were at Step 1. Write their name. 3. Pray for that person specifically every day for 7 days before approaching them. ...

quiz.question: According to 2 Chronicles 7:1-2 KJV what happened when the glory of the LORD filled Solomon's temple — and what does this picture?
choices: The priests completed their ministry and departed in an orderly fashion
The fire consumed the sacrifice and the glory filled the house — and the priests could not enter to minister because the glory exceeded what prepared flesh could stand in
The glory appeared visibly to the people assembled but the priests continued their functions normally

The priests received a special anointing that enabled them to minister more effectively than before 2 Chronicles 7:1-2 — the fire came down, the glory filled the house, the priests could not stand to minister. Not because they were unprepared — because what arrived exceeded what any prepared flesh could remain upright in. This is the picture of Pentecost — the same elements, the same God, the same pattern of the filled vessel exceeding the capacity of the flesh to contain it.

quiz.question: According to Acts 2:1-4 KJV what were the three elements present at Pentecost — and how do they connect to Solomon's temple?
choices: Preaching, prayer, and praise — the three elements of the apostolic worship model
Wind, fire, and filling — the same elements as the temple dedication, the same God, the same pattern a thousand years later
Light, sound, and anointing — the three signs of genuine revival

Speaking, hearing, and understanding — the three elements of the communication of the gospel Acts 2:1-4 — wind, fire, filled. The same elements as 2 Chronicles 7. The same God. The pattern was drawn a thousand years before Pentecost. The one accord of Acts 1:14 produced the availability. The suddenly of Acts 2:2 was God's timing.

quiz.question: According to Acts 2:38 KJV what are the four essential components of the great commission Peter delivered?
choices: Believe, confess, follow, and serve — the four steps of discipleship
Repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins — and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost
Hear, believe, pray, and receive — the four sequential acts of salvation

Turn, commit, surrender, and give — the four movements of genuine conversion Acts 2:38 — repent, be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. The great commission reduced to its essential components. Repentance is the turning. Baptism in the name of Jesus Christ is the obedience the name requires. Remission is the account settled. The gift of the Holy Ghost is the promise of the Father — the equipment the ambassador carries.

quiz.question: According to Ezekiel 22:30 KJV what was God seeking — and how does this describe the Step 12 ambassador's intercessory role?
choices: A man of great theological knowledge who could teach the people accurately
A man of recognized spiritual authority who could lead the nation in reform
A man who would stand in the gap before God for the land — the intercessor who prays specifically for the field before entering it

A man of pure moral character who would set an example for the surrounding nations Ezekiel 22:30 — God sought for a man to stand in the gap. The Step 12 ambassador stands in the gap for the specific person in the field — naming them, praying specifically, asking God to prepare the ground before the conversation arrives.

lessons.title: The ambassador — standing in the gap and carrying the great commission to the field
lessons.author: RRN Staff
lessons.body:
The ambassador — standing in the gap and carrying the great commission to the field ■ MEMBER — Login Required

In Step 1 we admitted we were powerless. What we carry now is the evidence that powerlessness was not the end of the story.

MEMBER LESSON — Step 12 Exam — GRADUATION Eight weeks ago Step 11 began with a direction — seek God. Today Step 12 closes with a commission — go. Between the seeking and the going — the clearing of the vessel, the maintaining of the daily walk, the positioning at the threshold, the examination of what is real, the establishment of what holds, the filling that turns the equipped from program graduates into ambassadors of the living God. Everything the steps built was pointing here.

WE ARE AMBASSADORS FOR CHRIST — 2 CORINTHIANS 5:20

"Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God." — 2 Corinthians 5:20 KJV The ambassador does not represent himself. He represents the government that sent him — with the full weight of that government's authority behind every word he speaks. He does not travel on his own credibility. He carries the credentials of the One who commissioned him. He does not deliver his own message. He delivers the message of the One whose name is on the commission. The Step 12 person who understands ambassador does not approach the field saying here is what the program did for me. He says here is what God did in me through the obedience — and He is offering to do it in you too. The message is not the steps. The message is the God the steps were pointing toward. As though God did beseech you by us. The ambassador's voice is God's appeal reaching the person in the field through the cleared and filled vessel of the one standing in front of them. That is the weight of the commission. Not a recovery testimony. A divine appeal, delivered in person, by a person in whom the thing being offered is visibly real.

PAUL AND THE DISCIPLES WHO HAD NOT RECEIVED — ACTS 19:1-6

"And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples, he said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost." — Acts 19:1-2 KJV Paul walked up to disciples. People who had believed. People who had been baptized — in John's baptism, the baptism of repentance. Genuine faith. Genuine obedience to what they understood. And Paul asked the question before he assumed the answer. Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? They had not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

Paul did not dismiss what they had. He did not start them over. He explained what was missing, baptized them in the name of the Lord Jesus, laid hands on them — and they received the Holy Ghost. This is the ambassador's model. Meet the person where they are. Affirm what is genuine. Ask the question before assuming the answer. And walk them toward what is still available. Every person the Step 12 ambassador reaches will be somewhere on this road. Some at the very beginning of Acts 19 — believing something but not yet knowing the full picture. Some baptized in a form that was not the name. Some who have done everything except receive what God promises the obedient. The ambassador does not judge where they are. The ambassador walks them toward what they have not yet received.

DISCIPLING OTHERS IN PRACTICAL WAYS — 2 TIMOTHY 2:2

"And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also." — 2 Timothy 2:2 KJV The multiplication of Step 12 is not mass outreach. It is one person committed to faithful relationship with one person who will do something with what is given — who will eventually commit the same to another faithful person who will teach others also. Four generations in one verse. What was received — committed — to those who will teach — others also. The chain does not break if every link in it takes 2 Timothy 2:2 seriously. The practical discipleship looks like: sitting with the person in Step 1 who cannot name what is broken. Walking beside the person in Step 4 who is afraid of what the inventory will find. Reviewing the Step 8 list with the person who wants to protect one name on it. The phone answered at 11pm. The hard question asked honestly. These are the daily unglamorous acts of the multiplication that 2 Timothy 2:2 produces over a generation.

GUARDING YOUR FAITH WHILE POURING INTO OTHERS — 1 CORINTHIANS 9:27

Paul wrote this to people in the church at Corinth who had received what God promises the obedient — warning those already born again into the covenant life about the specific danger of neglecting their own walk while pouring into others: "But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway." — 1 Corinthians 9:27 KJV Paul named the specific danger of the Step 12 life: preaching to others while the body is not under subjection. The ambassador who pours into others without maintaining the personal examination and disciplines is the most vulnerable person in the field. The maintenance is the protection. Keep the daily Word. Keep the daily prayer. Keep the Step 10 inventory. Keep the Step 11 posture. Keep the examination of 2 Corinthians 13:5 active — not only at the beginning of Step 12 but every week of the commissioned life. The person who examines themselves regularly cannot be taken by surprise. The person who has stopped examining is already drifting and does not yet know it.

THE HONEST QUESTION BEFORE YOU LEAVE

Two kinds of graduates sit in this room.

The disciples were in a locked room when the risen Christ appeared. Not on a mountaintop. Not in the temple. In a locked room, afraid. He came through the walls. The commission came before the fear was gone.

The first: the person for whom the examination confirmed the faith is real, the establishment made it stable, the baptism of the Holy Ghost came, the expression has begun, and the expansion is already in motion. That person is an ambassador. The equipment is present. The commission is active. Go. The Lord will work with you. Mark 16:20 — they went forth and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them. The second: the person who recognizes — honestly, in the quiet of this moment — that the baptism of the Holy Ghost has not yet come. That the examination found something unaddressed. That Acts 1:14 is still their assignment. That person is not a failure. They are exactly where the disciples Paul found in Acts 19 were — genuine in what they have, not yet having received what is still available. The road is not closed. The door is still open. "Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me." — Revelation 3:20 KJV Return to what was not fully given. Give it fully. Position again in the place of Acts 1:14. Ask as Luke 11:13 instructs — how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask. The obedience that opens the door is still available. And God is still the author of eternal salvation to those who obey Him.

THE FINAL WORD OF THE CURRICULUM — ACTS 2:38-39

THE HONEST QUESTION BEFORE YOU LEAVE

"Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call." — Acts 2:38-39 KJV This is where the curriculum ends — because this is where the road that leads to it begins. The commission Peter stood up and preached has not changed. It has not been updated or revised. It is the same message to the same field: Repentance — the actual turning toward God, not the feeling of sorrow alone. Baptism in the name of Jesus Christ — the obedience of water baptism in the name, as commanded. Remission of sins — the record cleared through the blood of Christ applied in obedience. The gift of the Holy Ghost — the promise of the Father, given to the obedient, still available, still real. The ambassador carries this message. Not as the summary of what the program produced. As the offer of what God promises to every person who hears it and obeys. And to all that are afar off. The person in Step 1 who does not yet know there is a road. The person in the far country who has not yet come to themselves. The person whose wreckage is still accumulating. The person whose Step 1 has not yet happened — whose admission of powerlessness is still somewhere ahead on a road they cannot see. That person is the field. That person is for whom Acts 2:39 was written. And the promise is unto them — the same promise that was unto you when you did not yet know it existed. You are the ambassador. You have the testimony. You carry the message.
"And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following." — Mark 16:20 KJV The Lord working with them. Not for them. With them. The same God who authored the salvation, who filled the upper room, who sent the fire from heaven, who bore witness with the Spirit — working with the ambassador who has been filled and commissioned and sent. Walk it out faithfully. THE NAME UPON THE AMBASSADOR "And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads." — Revelation 22:4 KJV The final vision of the Scripture closes with the same pattern that opened in Numbers 6:27 — the Name upon the people of God. Not upon a building. Not upon an institution. Upon the people — specifically, permanently, visibly. The name that was placed in baptism is the name that remains in the final state of the redeemed. What the water applied, eternity confirms. The ambassador who goes out in Step 12 carries this name. Not as a badge but as an identity. Not as a slogan but as the covenant relationship in which they stand and from which they speak. Every person they lead through the twelve steps is being led toward the same door they stood at in Step 11 L4 — the door of the promise of the Father, the filling that the steps have been clearing the way for, the name that God places upon the people He calls His own. "Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all." — 1 Corinthians 12:4-6 KJV Paul wrote this to born-again believers in Corinth — showing them that the same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God produces diverse operations in diverse people. Not every person's experience of the road looks identical. Not every person's expression of the gifted life takes the same form. But the same Spirit governs all of it — and the same evidence of His arrival confirms it. The ambassador does not require every person on the road to have arrived at the same point, at the same pace, through the same specific experience. They meet every person where they are — as the Acts 19 pattern shows: when Paul found disciples at Ephesus, he asked what they had received and walked them toward what was available that they had not yet received. That is the ambassador's posture: affirm what is genuine, name what is available, walk with the person toward the threshold. "And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following." — Mark 16:20 KJV They went forth. The Lord worked with them. The word was confirmed by what followed it. The ambassador does not go alone. The Comforter who abides goes with them. The name under which they go is the name above every name. The word they carry is confirmed by the same Spirit who filled the upper room on the day the promise arrived.

THE FAMILY NAME — THE CURRICULUM'S FINAL WORD ON THE NAME

Every person who has come through this program knows something about names. They arrived carrying the names the addiction had confirmed — the ones given without authority by people who did not have the right to name them, the ones they gave themselves in the worst moments, the ones the family line produced before they made their first choice. They have done the work of examining those names — in the inventory, in the confession, in the amends, in the daily examination. They have discovered in the process something the addiction never offered: the possibility of a name that was not produced by the flesh, not inherited from the first Adam, not carved into them by what was done to them in rooms they could not leave. The curriculum began with a seed in the first lesson: God places His name on His people. That seed has grown through every step. It grew in the preface — Numbers 6:27, the name placed on Israel through the priestly blessing. It deepened in Step 2 — Isaiah 45:4, God surnameing His people though they had not known Him. It obligated in Step 8 — 2 Chronicles 7:14, the people called by His name who must live accordingly. It arrived at the threshold in Step 11 — the full progressive revelation from El Shaddai through Jehovah to the one name that contains them all. "For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named." — Ephesians 3:14-15 KJV The whole family. In heaven and earth. Named. Not after a program. Not after a tradition. After the Father — whose name, revealed at last in the Son, is Jesus. The family name is the name above every name. And every person who has entered through the covenant act the Son established bears that name. Not as a label. As identity, authority, ownership, belonging. As a name that does not expire when the circumstances change or when the person fails to maintain their performance. A name is the person. In Scripture, to bear a name is to bear the one who gave it — their character, their authority, their will. "And all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the LORD." — Deuteronomy 28:10 KJV. The name is visible. It distinguishes. It marks the one who bears it as belonging to the One who placed it. The ambassador of Step 12 goes into the field carrying this name. Not as a doctrine to argue. As a living testimony — the evidence of what the name produces in the life of a person it has been placed on. The names the addiction confirmed are no longer the last word. The name above every name is. "Arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord." — Acts 22:16 KJV This is the invitation that does not close. It was extended to Paul after three days of prayer. It was extended to the Ephesian disciples who had genuine faith but had not yet received. It is extended to every person who has walked this road — who has arrived at the end of what the first Adam's inheritance can produce and is ready to enter the last Adam's. The name is Jesus. The covenant act is baptism in that name. The promise that follows is the gift of the Holy Ghost. Not three separate options from a menu. One entry into one covenant, received by one obedient people, marked by one name. That is the final word of this curriculum. Walk it out faithfully.

They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. That is the pattern of Step 12. Not by performance. Not by perfection. By what God has done, and the honest account of it.

THE STEWARD — GIVING AS EVIDENCE OF GENUINE TRANSFORMATION

The person who has been genuinely changed does not give because they are required to. They give because the transformation that began in Step 1 has worked its way into every area of life — including how they hold what God has provided.

"Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine." — Proverbs 3:9–10 KJV

The firstfruits principle is not primarily a financial instruction. It is a statement about governance. The person who gives the first portion back to God is the person who has genuinely accepted that what they have is not theirs to manage alone. The first goes back. The rest is held in the same spirit.

Zacchaeus did not give because he was told to. He stood and said: the half of my goods I give to the poor. The transformation produced the giving. The giving was the evidence. Step 12 is lived by the person who has understood this — that what God has done in them works its way outward into how they steward everything He has placed in their hands.

THE LONG-TERM LIFE — WHAT YEAR FIVE LOOKS LIKE

The person who has completed all twelve steps once has completed the beginning.

The steps are not a one-time course. They are the description of a life. The person who works Step 1 honestly will work it again — not because the first time did not count, but because the flesh does not retire and the life that was genuinely surrendered in Step 3 requires the ongoing maintenance of Steps 10 and 11 to remain genuinely surrendered.

What does the long-term life of Step 12 actually look like?

It looks like Step 10 in the morning — the daily examination before the day has added its layers of rationalization and self-justification. The person five years out who has maintained the daily inventory is a different person than the one who did it for the first ninety days and then assumed they no longer needed it.

It looks like Step 11 before the phone — the choice, made daily, to bring the mind before God before the world has access to it. The person five years out who maintains the morning discipline is the person whose Step 12 service comes from a place of genuine contact with God, not from memory of what that contact used to feel like.

It looks like Step 12 in the ordinary — not the dramatic rescue, not the crisis intervention, but the steady presence of a person who shows up for the person who has not shown up yet. The person who was rescued is the person who does the rescuing. Not because they have arrived. Because they have not forgotten where they started.

"Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted." — Galatians 6:1 KJV

Considering thyself. The person five years out who restores the one overtaken in a fault does so in the spirit of meekness — knowing that the fault they are restoring from is the fault they themselves were overtaken by, not long ago. That meekness is not false humility. It is the honest memory of where Step 1 began.

The long-term life of Step 12 is not the life of a person who has outgrown the program. It is the life of a person who has grown into it — who understands that the maintenance is the service, the service is the maintenance, and the person who walks this road faithfully for five years is the person the newcomer at Step 1 will one day point to and say: that is what I am walking toward.

Walk it out faithfully.

THE DAILY RHYTHM OF THE PERSON WHO HAS COMPLETED THE STEPS

The completed life of Step 12 is not a graduate life — it is a maintained life. The rhythm that sustains it is the same rhythm the steps built, now practiced not as a program requirement but as the natural cadence of a person who knows what the absence of that rhythm produces.

Morning: the Word before anything else. Not because it is a rule but because the person who has maintained Step 11 across years has discovered what the person who neglects it rediscovers regularly — the unguarded mind is the vulnerable mind, and the mind brought before God before the day begins is governed differently than the mind that comes to God after the world has had its say.

Daily: the promptly principle of Step 10. When wrong, admit it — in the hour, not the week. The longer the gap between the wrong and the acknowledgment, the more the flesh builds the justification that makes the acknowledgment feel unnecessary. The person five years out who still practices Step 10 daily is the person whose relationships bear the evidence of it.

Weekly: the gathering. The person who served others through Step 12 needs the same community they now serve in. No one maintains this road alone. The person five years out who is still in the room — still sitting with the person at Step 1 — is both serving and being sustained by the service. The room that saved them is the room they are now keeping open.

Ongoing: the testimony. The word of their testimony (Revelation 12:11 KJV) is not a fixed document produced at graduation. It is the living account of a life that continues to be changed. The person five years out has five more years of testimony than they had at the beginning. That testimony is the most powerful thing they carry — and it only grows more powerful as the years confirm what God has done.

TABITHA — THE LEGACY THAT FOLLOWED THE CHANGED LIFE

"Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did." — Acts 9:36 KJV When Tabitha died, the widows of Joppa stood weeping and showing Peter the coats and garments she had made. The evidence of her life was in the hands of the people who had received it. She had not recovered privately. She had lived in a way that left a tangible record in the lives of the people around her — in the clothing on their backs, in the provision she had given, in the company of people who had received what her hands produced. Peter prayed. Tabitha opened her eyes and sat up. Peter presented her alive to the community. And the record says: it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord. The recovery that ends in isolation — the person who gets clean and stays to themselves, who guards their healing carefully and offers nothing outward — has not yet understood what Tabitha's life demonstrates. The changed life produces tangible evidence in the lives of the people who touch it. Coats and garments. Works and almsdeeds. Things that remain in the hands of the people who received them after the person who gave them has left the room. The ambassador of Step 12 does not graduate into a private maintenance of their own healing. They graduate into a Tabitha life — full of good works, producing things that remain in the hands of the people they serve, living in a way that the widows of Joppa will stand and show what their hands produced.

The person who has walked all twelve steps honestly is not the person who arrived at Step 1. That is not an exaggeration — it is the testimony Scripture promises to those who walk the road faithfully. They overcame. Not they tried to overcome. They overcame.

TEACHER NOTES

Step 12 Lesson 4 — Graduation THE MOST PASTORALLY DEMANDING SESSION OF THE CURRICULUM. Handle with gravity and genuine pastoral care. This is not a ceremony. It is the final honest accounting before the commission is given. 2 CORINTHIANS 5:20 — AMBASSADORS FOR CHRIST: Open with this. The ambassador does not represent himself. Ask students: when you enter the conversation in the field — whose message are you carrying? Whose authority are you representing? The person who answers that with clarity ...

SCRIPTURE MEMORY

■ Acts 2:38 KJV — "Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost."

■ Acts 2:39 KJV — "For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off."

■ 2 Corinthians 5:20 KJV — "Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us."

■ Mark 16:20 KJV — "And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them."

■ Hebrews 5:9 KJV — "And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him."

ASSIGNMENT

GRADUATION — The final accounting and the commission BEFORE THE FINAL EXAM — complete this honestly: 1. Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? Answer honestly in writing: A. "Yes — here is the specific evidence in my life: ___. I am commissioned to go as an ambassador for Christ." B. "Not yet — I am in the posture of Acts 1:14. Here is what that looks like specifically for me this week...

quiz.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:20 KJV what is the nature of the ambassador's commission — and whose message does the ambassador carry?
choices: The ambassador carries their personal testimony — the power comes from the authenticity of their story
The ambassador carries the program — the twelve steps are the message being delivered
We are ambassadors for Christ — as though God did beseech by us, delivering God's appeal for reconciliation in Christ's stead

The ambassador carries the church's doctrine — representing the theological position of their community 2 Corinthians 5:20 — we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us. The ambassador does not represent himself or the program. He represents the God who commissioned him, delivering a divine appeal for reconciliation through the cleared and filled vessel of his life. The message is not the steps. The message is the God the steps were pointing toward.

quiz.question: According to Acts 19:1-2 KJV what question did Paul ask the disciples he found — and what does this model for the Step 12 ambassador?
choices: He asked if they had been baptized — modeling that baptism is the first question to establish
He asked how long they had believed — modeling that the length of faith determines its depth
He asked have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed — modeling that the ambassador asks before assuming and walks people toward what they have not yet received

He asked what church they attended — modeling that community connection is the priority question Acts 19:1-2 — have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? Paul asked the question before assuming the answer.

quiz.question: According to Acts 2:38-39 KJV what is the final word of this curriculum — and to whom does the promise extend?
choices: Repent and believe — the promise extends to those who confess Christ sincerely and ask Him into their heart
Repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost — unto you and your children and all that are afar off
Confess and receive — the promise extends to all who sincerely seek God in prayer

Believe and be baptized — the promise extends to those who join the community of believers Acts 2:38-39 — repent, be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, for the remission of sins, receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. The sinner\'s prayer — asking Jesus into the heart or confessing Christ sincerely — is not found in the apostolic record. Every commission in Acts results in the same complete response: repentance, baptism in Jesus name for remission of sins, and the gift of the Holy Ghost.

quiz.question: According to Mark 16:20 KJV what accompanied the disciples who went forth — and what does this promise the Step 12 ambassador?
choices: Large crowds and immediate results — confirming the effectiveness of the gospel message
Protection from all opposition — the Lord shielded them from every threat
The Lord working with them and confirming the word with signs following — the same God active through the ambassador who goes in His name

Specific instructions for each situation — the Lord directing every conversation in real time Mark 16:20 — they went forth and the Lord worked with them, confirming the word with signs following. Not for them. With them. The same God who filled the upper room and sent the fire from heaven works with the ambassador who has been filled and commissioned and sent. The graduation is not the conclusion. It is the launch.

quiz.question: What is the final honest question graduation asks — and what is the road forward for each of the two kinds of graduates?
choices: Did you complete the program — those who did are sent, those who did not repeat the year
Have ye received the Holy Ghost — those who have are ambassadors commissioned to go; those who have not are directed to the posture of Acts 1:14 and the door that is still open
Are you ready — those who feel ready are sent, those who do not wait until the feeling comes

Did you help someone else — those who did have multiplied, those who did not continue in Step 11 The honest question is Acts 19:2 applied personally — have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? Those who have are commissioned ambassadors. Those who have not are not failures — they are in the position of the Acts 19 disciples, genuine in what they have, with the receiving still available. The posture of Acts 1:14 is their next step. The door of Revelation 3:20 is still open. Both are loved. Both have a road forward.
